title_en: Koufu Food Company v. Korea Enterprise Bank and Bank of China, Nuclear Power Plant Sub-branch — dispute over letter of credit
ruling_gist_en: Fraud in letters of credit refers to conduct in which the beneficiary of a letter of credit, having no goods at all or being unable to deliver goods of inferior quality, individually or in malicious collusion with others, forges one or more types of documents that comply with the requirements of the letter of credit, thereby extracting payment under the letter of credit from the issuing bank, causing economic loss to the applicant for the letter of credit. An issuing bank, in the absence of evidence that the documents under the letter of credit were forged by the beneficiary individually or in malicious collusion with others for the purpose of extracting payment under the letter of credit from the issuing bank, and where such forgery has not caused substantial harm to the applicant for the letter of credit, may not invoke the fraud exception principle to letters of credit to refuse payment under the letter of credit.
